model: Deal-weighted scenario DCF (owner-FCF component mechanics per scenario via scripts/dcf_engine.py's project()/terminal_value(); scenarios framed as deal-completes/deal-breaks per dcf-methods SKILL.md routing for a live takeover situation, not growth-rate variants) -- hand-authored JSON built with the engine's own functions for exact fidelity, not the Drivers/build-dcf CLI path, because the takeover overlay needs scenario-specific narrative framing that the generic component engine's single global equity_bridge cannot express

inputs.sbc_source: Immaterial (share-based payment reserve well under $0.15m/yr historically, $0 in H1 FY2026 per BRW.NZ_Metrics.csv); treated as SBC-zero market -- house and street bases coincide
inputs.share_count_basis: 70.66m shares on issue at FY2026 (30 June 2026); diluted weighted-average 71.24m used only as a cross-check -- SBC is immaterial so the difference does not matter materially
inputs.wacc_rationale: NZD-built WACC for a small, sub-scale, loss-making NZ industrial in a live control contest: base 14.5%, bull 12.5%, bear 17.0%. Consistent with comparable NZ small-cap cyclical/turnaround precedents in this folder (MPG.NZ 13.5%, SVR.NZ 16.5%, AGL.NZ 17.0%) -- BRW.NZ sits at the higher end given governance instability (multiple board resignations, unresolved control contest), repeated guidance misses (H1 FY26 walk-back), and structurally negative current profitability.
inputs.lease_treatment: Lease costs are embedded inside the assumed EBITDA/EBIT margin paths as an ordinary operating cost (the component build works off assumed margins, not a reported OCF/capex base), so lease_cost_pct_path is left at 0 to avoid double-counting -- the margin paths already reflect a business that pays IFRS-16 lease costs out of EBIT. Lease liabilities ($16.2m at H1 FY26) are NOT included in net_debt -- net_debt is bank borrowings (nil) less cash (22.0m) only, per the ticker brief's instruction that IFRS-16 lease liabilities are tracked separately in kpis.
inputs.nci_treatment: None -- Bremworth has no reported non-controlling interests.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE: dcf-methods SKILL.md routes 'Live takeover, scheme, strategic review' to deal-completes vs deal-breaks weighting, not three growth-rate scenarios. Applied here: BEAR = turnaround stalls / any control transaction lapses (standalone melt-down economics, high WACC, thin/negative terminal value); BASE = turnaround delivers per FY27 guidance broadly on schedule (the more likely near-term path given the board-recommended, IAR-supported Mangawhai Collective offer signals management/board confidence and MCL/concert party already hold ~52% effective support); BULL = turnaround beats guidance and/or a renewed full-company strategic bid emerges (Floorscape/Mohawk previously offered up to 95c-$1.05 whole-company before the scheme collapsed on shareholder opposition, not on valuation grounds). Each scenario's intrinsic_value is a VERIFIABLE standalone owner-FCF-style component DCF (revenue growth x EBITDA margin path (EBIT margin + D&A%), D&A, capex, cash tax, discounted at scenario WACC, Gordon/cap-multiple terminal value via scripts/dcf_engine.py) so the dashboard slider engine can reconstruct it from assumptions. The live deal economics (90c partial offer within Clarien's 87c-$1.07 IAR range, prior 95c-$1.05 Floorscape whole-company terms) are NOT smuggled into intrinsic_value -- they inform the SCENARIO PROBABILITY WEIGHTS and are reported as an explicit cross-check (valuation_philosophy.deal_cross_check) because the engine's equity_bridge mechanism is a single GLOBAL total applied identically to all three scenarios (scripts/dcf_engine.py _Scenario.bridge), which cannot express a deal premium that differs by scenario the way this situation requires. FY2026 figures are from the 31-Aug-2026 unaudited preliminary results release, not an audited annual report (no FY2026 balance sheet/cash-flow statement extracted yet) -- OCF/capex/FCF are blank in BRW.NZ_Metrics.csv for FY2026 and the DCF is therefore built on revenue/EBIT margin fundamentals rather than a historical owner-FCF base year (there is no positive owner-FCF year to CAGR from in any case -- see historical_growth notes).

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Revenue, EPS and FCF CAGRs are not meaningful growth-rate inputs for this ticker: (1) revenue has been volatile and non-monotonic (FY2020 118.0 -> FY2024 80.3 -> FY2026 106.6, with FY2025/26 growth driven by the low-margin Elco Direct wool-trading channel, not the core carpet business recovering); (2) EPS is not usable -- net income has been negative in 6 of the last 10 fiscal years and FY2025's positive EPS was a $42.2m one-off Cyclone Gabrielle insurance receipt, not operating profit; (3) FCF has never been consistently positive on an owner-FCF basis, so no CAGR exists to select. selected_growth_rate (3.0%, base case near-term) is a judgment call built from the FY27 guidance narrative and Elco Direct's structurally higher but lower-margin revenue contribution, not derived from historical CAGRs -- see assumptions.base.growth_rates for the full component path.

entry_price.note: Entry prices are built on the STANDALONE component DCF flows at a 15% hurdle -- they are deliberately conservative relative to the live 90c offer price and do not incorporate deal-completion probability. A buyer using this DCF's discipline would not chase the current 0.70 price on fundamentals alone; the 90c board-recommended offer is a separate, nearer-dated realisation event, not a substitute for the hurdle discipline.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Base carries the plurality (45%) because the Mangawhai Collective offer is board-recommended and inside the independent adviser's 87c-$1.07 range, and MCL/concert party already control ~52% effective support -- this is the most probable near-term path for the register even though the offer covers only 44% of shares. Bear is held meaningfully high (30%, above the house default 15-25%) because Bremworth has repeatedly missed its own turnaround guidance (H1 FY26 explicitly walked back a promised H2 profitability/cash-flow-positive target), gross margin DETERIORATED in H1 FY26 (14.9% vs 21% pcp) rather than improving, and normalised losses, while narrowing, remain substantial (-$9.4m FY26 EBIT) with no confirmed demand-cycle catalyst. Bull is held at 25%, below house default, because the more lucrative Floorscape/Mohawk whole-company deal (up to 95c-$1.05) has already collapsed once on shareholder opposition (not valuation grounds), so a bull re-rate via a renewed full bid is plausible but not the base case.
probability_weighted.band_position_note: SBC is immaterial for BRW.NZ (NZD small-cap, no meaningful equity award expense) -- house and street bases coincide, so band_position is not meaningful and is reported as null rather than a degenerate 0.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Bremworth is a loss-making NZ premium carpet manufacturer (plus the fast-growing but low-margin Elco Direct wool-trading channel) mid-way through a multi-year operational turnaround, currently the subject of a live, board-recommended partial takeover offer. This is NOT a standard positive-FCF owner-FCF DCF: normalised EBIT has been negative every year since FY2025 restated (-$15.9m FY25, -$9.4m FY26), FY2025's headline GAAP profit was entirely a $42.2m Cyclone Gabrielle insurance receipt (underlying normalised EBITDA FY2025 was -$13.2m), and H1 FY26 showed the turnaround has not yet delivered -- gross margin fell to 14.9% from 21% pcp. Per dcf-methods SKILL.md's routing table, a live takeover/scheme situation is valued via deal-completes-vs-deal-breaks scenario weighting, not growth-rate variants of a single business-as-usual case.
valuation_philosophy.methodology: Each of the three scenarios is an internally-consistent, independently-verifiable standalone owner-FCF-style component DCF (10-year explicit horizon -- needed because margins are still normalising well past year 5 -- discounted at a scenario-specific NZD WACC, Gordon-growth terminal value capped by an EV/EBITDA multiple, built with scripts/dcf_engine.py's own project()/terminal_value() functions). BEAR represents the turnaround stalling and/or the current takeover process lapsing without a further control transaction (as the earlier Floorscape/Mohawk scheme did in July 2026): flat-to-slow revenue, EBIT margin improving only slowly from -8% toward breakeven over 10 years, 17% WACC. BASE represents the turnaround delivering broadly per FY27 guidance (Napier plant fully online, cost-out programme flowing through, SDN synthetic range contributing): EBIT margin reaching a sustainable ~4% by year 5-6, 14.5% WACC. BULL represents the turnaround beating guidance and/or a renewed full-company strategic bid: EBIT margin reaching ~6% (still modest vs. pre-cyclone historic peaks), 12.5% WACC. Net debt is negative $22.0m (nil bank borrowings, $22.0m available cash net of $4.9m restricted cash held as bank-guarantee security) -- BRW.NZ's clean balance sheet is the key source of downside protection and turnaround runway.
valuation_philosophy.deal_cross_check: The live Mangawhai Collective partial offer (90c/share for 44% of shares not already held, board-recommended, within independent adviser Clarien Partners' 87c-$1.07 valuation range) and the prior, now-lapsed Floorscape/Mohawk whole-company approach (revised to 95c after NZCC clearance, indicative range previously guided to $0.95-1.05 total consideration before lapsing on shareholder opposition in July 2026 -- NOT on valuation grounds, a ~38% bloc simply preferred to retain control) together establish a market-tested value corridor of roughly 87c-$1.07 for full or majority control. This DCF's standalone BASE intrinsic value ($0.38) and even BULL ($0.85) sit BELOW this corridor, and the probability-weighted IV ($0.40) sits well below both the corridor and the current price ($0.70). This gap is expected and informative, not an error: (1) the IAR range and the Floorscape/MCL offer prices are CONTROL-PREMIUM, deal-informed valuations (an acquirer capturing 100% control and optionality this minority-shareholder DCF cannot capture) rather than standalone going-concern values at an arm's-length discount rate; (2) FY26 tangible book value (~$0.85/share estimated at 30 June 2026, extrapolating H1 FY26 equity of $65.4m less the implied H2 net loss) sits inside the IAR floor, consistent with the IAR anchoring substantially to book/asset value plus modest going-concern upside rather than to a high-growth DCF; (3) the standalone DCF is deliberately built at a demanding hurdle-adjacent discount rate on a business with a real, documented history of guidance misses -- it is not intended to match a board-recommended takeover price, and should not be read as calling the 90c offer 'too cheap' or 'too rich'. A shareholder's decision to accept the 90c offer is better informed by the IAR and the offer's own conditions than by this standalone DCF, which exists to answer a different question: what is this business worth as a continuing, independent going concern to a patient minority holder who does NOT tender.
key_risks_to_valuation: Execution risk: Bremworth has repeatedly missed its own turnaround targets, most recently walking back a promised H2 FY26 return to profitability/positive operating cash flow at the February 2026 half-year result -- the base case assumes FY27 guidance is met this time

Demand cycle: NZ/Australia residential construction and renovation activity has been weak for years with no confirmed recovery catalyst or timeline; every scenario is sensitive to when (or whether) this turns

Competitive scale: Godfrey Hirst (Mohawk-owned) makes roughly double Bremworth's wool carpet volumes with a well-capitalised parent -- structurally limits Bremworth's pricing power and margin ceiling in the core carpet category

Elco Direct concentration: FY26 revenue growth was overwhelmingly Elco Direct wool-trading volume/price driven (a 'seismic shift' in export demand) -- this is a lower-margin, potentially less durable growth driver than a genuine carpet-demand recovery, and the base/bull cases assume it does not reverse

Takeover process risk: the Mangawhai Collective offer is not yet formal (as of the 31-Aug release) and is a PARTIAL offer for only 44% of shares -- accepting shareholders may be scaled back and minority holders who do not tender remain exposed to a controlling-shareholder structure without full exit liquidity; the more lucrative Floorscape whole-company route has already failed once

Balance sheet runway: FY26 operating cash outflow (ex-insurance items) was still $(9.3)m despite a $14.5m YoY improvement -- against $22.0m available cash this gives roughly 2+ years of runway at the current burn rate before a raise would be needed if the turnaround stalls, which is the central bear-case risk
